title: Database migration review
summary: Review schema and data migrations for compatibility, recovery and irreversible effects before they run, including the identifiers that must not change without a migration.

provenance.notes: Ties to this repository's rule that persisted identifiers and table names change only together with an explicit migration.

inputs.name: migration
inputs.description: The migration and the code that reads the changed data.

outputs.name: assessment
outputs.description: Compatibility window, rollback plan and irreversible effects.

workflow.step: Enumerate everything that reads or writes the changed tables, columns, files or identifiers.
workflow.check: Readers and writers come from a code search.

workflow.step: Define the compatibility window: old code with new schema and new code with old schema must both be safe, or the deploy order must be explicit.
workflow.check: Rollback of code does not corrupt migrated data.

workflow.step: Classify each statement reversible or irreversible; for irreversible ones require a backup or a stated recovery path.
Check backfills are batched, restartable and idempotent.
workflow.check: Running the migration twice is harmless.

workflow.step: Verify the migration on a copy or fixture and record the command and result.

constraints: Do not run migrations against live data from an analysis task.
Persisted identifiers and table names change only with an explicit migration and review.
Treat a missing recovery step as a blocker.

examples.title: Rename a column
examples.situation: A column is renamed in one release.
examples.guidance: Add the new column, dual-write, backfill, switch reads, then drop the old column in a later release.

verification: Each statement is marked reversible or irreversible with recovery noted.
The compatibility window is stated in terms of deploy order.

task.text: Review the migration: alter table, backfill and the irreversible data migration.
Plan the schema change to rename column in the persisted table.
